title: A mobile sound localization setup
author: Wasmann, Janssen, et al.
materials: The target-response plots are the standard way of presenting the data, of course, further analysis of the data is possible. For instance, in case of asymmetric hearing loss or unilaterally aided patients, Vogt et al. [22] calculated the gains, biases, and MAE for the stimuli presented to the left and right side separately. Furthermore, the response times can be analyzed, which could be a proxy for task difficulty.

steps.title: Save trial data in Matlab
steps.instruction: For each trial, record the stimulus settings (azimuth, elevation, frequency, duration) and the raw head‑movement data (azimuth, elevation, response time) in a Matlab data structure and save the structure after the trial for later offline analysis.

steps.title: Online visualization and detection
steps.instruction: During measurement, plot the head position (in degrees) and head velocity (in 100° · s⁻¹) versus time (seconds) in real time; the software automatically detects the movement start and end points, which can be manually corrected later if needed.

substeps.instruction: Plot head azimuth and elevation over time (degrees vs seconds).
Plot head velocity over time (100° · s⁻¹ vs seconds).
Automatically detect initiation and termination of each head movement.
Allow offline manual correction of detected start/end points.

steps.title: Generate preliminary target-response plots
steps.instruction: After each block of trials, automatically create preliminary target‑response plots for azimuth and elevation that display all completed trials.

steps.title: Correct data and compute final fit
steps.instruction: When the block is finished, review all measurements, manually correct any erroneous start‑ or end‑points, then generate a final target‑response plot for the block and fit a linear model using αRESP = a·αTARG + b and εRESP = c·εTARG + d.

substeps.instruction: Inspect all recorded movements for errors.
Create the final target‑response plot for the block.
Perform linear regression separately for azimuth (α) and elevation (ε) using the equation above.

steps.title: Calculate mean absolute error
steps.instruction: Compute the mean absolute error (MAE) for azimuth using MAE = (1/n) ∑_{i=1}^{n} |α_iRESP − α_iTARG|.
